name: @projexlight/connector-jira
summary: Jira Cloud connector: OAuth install + bidirectional issue / sprint / board sync. Sit alongside sdk-workflow + sdk-approval so an internal ProjexCloud task transitions to a real Jira issue (and vice versa) without leaving either system. Foundation for engineering + IT ops blueprints.

events.name: connector-jira.binding.created.v1
events.description: Entity binding registered (ProjexCloud task ↔ Jira issue type).

events.name: connector-jira.webhook.received.v1
events.description: Jira webhook ingested (issue_created, issue_updated, sprint_started, etc.).

hooks.name: registerBinding
hooks.description: Bind a ProjexCloud entity → Jira issue type.

scenarios.title: Tenant connects their Jira Cloud site
scenarios.when_to_use: First install. Admin grants OAuth scopes; connector stores refresh token + records site_id.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Install row + vault-wrapped refresh token. Emits .install.created.v1.

scenarios.title: ProjexCloud task creates a Jira issue automatically
scenarios.when_to_use: Reactive on workflow.run.started.v1 — bind 'engineering-tasks' workflow → 'ACME / Story' issue type so engineering work shows up in their existing backlog.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Issue created in Jira; ID stored on the ProjexCloud task. Updates flow both ways via .webhook.received.v1.

scenarios.title: Pull active sprint → ProjexCloud sprint dashboard
scenarios.when_to_use: Daily pull of sprint state so the ProjexCloud sprint dashboard reflects what's actually in Jira.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Hourly pull hydrates jira_sprint + projects into sdk-projection.sprint.

scenarios.title: Jira issue transitions to 'Done' → close ProjexCloud task
scenarios.when_to_use: Webhook receives 'issue_updated' with new status 'Done'; we close the linked ProjexCloud task in lockstep.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Transition propagated; linked ProjexCloud task closes. Emits .webhook.received.v1 + downstream completion event.

scenarios.title: Scheduler keeps the OAuth refresh chain alive
scenarios.when_to_use: Atlassian refresh tokens expire after 90 days of inactivity; scheduler refreshes weekly for installs with low traffic.
scenarios.example_code: // driven by startScheduler — periodic refresh for low-traffic installs.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Install row's expires_at advances; no tenant-visible action.

compliance_posture.notes: Refresh tokens vault-wrapped. Webhook signature verification mandatory. EU sites pinned to atlassian-eu endpoints for residency.
